text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co said it exercised an option to extend a three-year research collaboration with Cadus Pharmaceutical Corp by an additional two years.
To date, Cadus has received over $30 million in equity and cash payments from Bristol-Myers, which owns about 17 percent of Cadus stock.
Through the extension period, Bristol-Myers said, it will provide Cadus with about $10 million in additional research funding.
As before, Cadus would receive specific milestone payments and royalties from any marketed products that result from the collaboration.
The original agreement was initiated in July 1994 and focuses on the discovery of drugs directed at G protein-coupled receptors, Bristol-Meyers said.

These receptors, which are found in the membranes of almost all cells, including human, animal, and plant cells, are known or suspected to play a role in diseases such as AIDS, hypertension, atherosclerosis, some cancers, and immunological disorders including rheumatoid arthritis.
Bristol-Myers said it is not only extending the agreement, but is expanding the scope of the partnership to include other molecular targets proprietary to Cadus.
"The extension of this collaboration is important for two reasons," said Leon E. Rosenberg, M.D., senior vice president, Scientific Affairs, Bristol- Myers Squibb.

"One, it's important because it demonstrates the increasing emphasis this company has on drug discovery in areas of unmet medical need; and two, it's important because it reflects the success of our collaboration so far.
